plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A cormous perennial that sends up crocus-like flowers in autumn, well after its leaves have died back. The goblet-shaped blooms emerge directly from the ground without foliage, and strap-like leaves appear the following spring. All parts are highly toxic.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Native to Europe, in damp meadows and woodland edges; widely cultivated in temperate gardens of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: It contains colchicine, a compound used in medicine to treat gout and by plant breeders to induce chromosome doubling in crops.

plants.name: Aster novae-angliae (Symphyotrichum novae-angliae)
plants.description: A tall, clump-forming perennial with hairy stems and dense clusters of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. It thrives in moist meadows and is a vital late-season nectar source for pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America in prairies, meadows and roadsides; cultivated in gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Monarch butterflies rely on New England asters for fuel during their autumn migration to Mexico.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A fast-growing deciduous to semi-evergreen tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in masses of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In spring the whole canopy turns violet and carpets the ground beneath with fallen blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), Argentina and New Zealand's northern regions
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its roughly 70,000 trees that bloom every October.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A popular perennial with many flower forms, from daisy-like to pompom and spider types. Short days trigger bud formation, making it a classic autumn bloomer in gardens and in cut-flower production.
plants.location: Originated in China and Japan; grown in gardens across temperate regions of Asia, Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for over 2,500 years, and the flower is the imperial emblem of Japan.

plants.name: Sternbergia lutea
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that produces bright, crocus-like golden flowers in autumn alongside its strap-shaped leaves. It thrives in sunny, dry, rocky Mediterranean habitats.
plants.location: Mediterranean region through Turkey and the Middle East to Iran; grown in rock gardens elsewhere
plants.funFact: It is often thought to be the biblical 'lily of the field' mentioned in the Gospels.
